items.title: Synchronized Double-Sided Printing System

items.title: Built-In Image Processor
items.desc: Integrated onboard image processing handles dual-side design data in real time, ensuring perfectly synchronized output between the front and back print engines without external processing delays.

items.title: Dual-Zone Drying System
items.desc: Rear-side IR panel (9 kW) combined with a dual-side forced air heater (18 kW) ensures both fabric faces are fully and evenly dried before collection, preventing smudging or colour transfer.

items.title: Yarn-Dye Effect Replication Technology

items.title: Optional Centering Device
items.desc: Automatic fabric centering add-on ensures consistent alignment entering the dual-side print zone, maintaining registration accuracy across varying fabric widths and roll conditions.

items.title: Industrial Power and Pneumatic Architecture
items.desc: 400V triphase power supply with 44 kW total installed capacity and 6 bar pneumatics ensures stable, consistent operation of both print carriages and the drying system under continuous production loads.

items.title: Supply Chain Efficiency

sections.heading: How a Double Sided Digital Textile Printer Works
paragraphs: Printing the back of fabric usually means rewinding, flipping and reloading the roll, then trying to line up the second print with the first. MAS Vertical runs the fabric vertically between two print carriages, one on each side, and prints both faces at the same time in a single pass.
Because the fabric never leaves the machine and both carriages move in sync, front-to-back registration stays accurate. Two drying stages set both prints before take-up.

subsections.heading: Three Ways to Print Both Sides
paragraphs: Print the same design on both sides for scarves, flags and curtains, or to replicate yarn-dyed checks and stripes. Print the same design in different colourways for reversible garments. Or print completely different designs on each face for reversible jackets, printed linings and denim with a printed inner face.

items.a: Woven fabrics where both faces matter, especially shirting, denim, scarves and home textiles. We'll run samples on your fabric.
Reactive or pigment for cotton, disperse for polyester. Our team will configure inks for your fabric range.
Load both designs as one job. The built-in image processor prepares them, the machine prints and dries both sides in line, and fixation follows your usual process.

faq.heading: MAS Vertical: Double Sided Digital Textile Printer

items.q: What is a double sided digital textile printer?
items.a: A double sided digital textile printer prints both faces of a fabric in a single pass. MAS Vertical runs the fabric vertically between two print carriages, one on each side, so the front and back are printed at the same time without rewinding, flipping or reloading the roll.

items.q: Can MAS Vertical print different designs on each side?
items.a: Yes. It prints two independent designs in one pass. You can print the same design on both sides, the same design in different colourways, or completely different designs on the front and back.

items.q: How accurate is the front-to-back registration?
items.a: Both sides are printed at the same time on the same fabric path by synchronised carriages. Since the fabric is never reloaded, the main cause of misregistration in two-pass printing is removed. An optional centering device helps keep the fabric edge steady on long runs.

items.q: What products is double-sided printing used for?
items.a: It's used for yarn-dyed-look shirting, reversible denim and garments, scarves, stoles and dupattas, curtains, flags and banners, which are all products seen from both sides.

items.q: What are the power and air requirements?
items.a: MAS Vertical needs a 400 V three-phase supply with 44 kW installed power, and compressed air at 6 bar with a maximum consumption of 20 litres per minute.

items.q: What print widths does it support?
items.a: It prints fabric from 900 mm up to 1,850 mm wide.
